items_missed: Set Agenda: never got or used the customer's name, never asked 'how are you today,' gave no agenda statement (what he'd cover / how long it'd take), no explicit 'sound good?' confirmation.

Probe: no zip codes for origin or destination, didn't ask about garage/storage/balcony, no storage stops or additional stops probed, never asked if there's anything the customer is worried about with the move.

Pricing/Differentiators: no 'pricing is super simple' opener, no hourly rate ever stated, no rundown of what's included (gas, truck, taxes, insurance, pads, tools), no disassembly/reassembly mention, no trip fee discussion, no No Worries Damage Coverage, no Meet Your Mover, no On-Time Guarantee, no 'no hidden fees' pitch — this entire section was essentially skipped.
Clock: never explained the clock starts on-site at contract signing, never mentioned the 2.5-hour minimum, no explicit sense-check ('does that make sense?').

Estimate: never stated how many movers or trucks are assigned, no drive-time/trip-fee variable addressed, no equivalents used (e.g. school-bus comparison), no assembly/disassembly note despite mentioning bed frame and other furniture.
Save Your Ass: entire section missing — no prep-before-move-day pitch, no consolidation examples, no 'take a carload' tip, no close.

Quote/Booking: no explicit 'no deposit required' mention, no confirmation-email handoff explained, no bolded-list-in-email mention, no 'reply with any corrections,' no 'any other questions before I let you go?', no hours/contact info given.
Politeness: never used the customer's name (Roy) once during the entire call.
Bonus: no rapport-building humor or personal moment, no insurance explanation (No Worries coverage + 60 cents/lb baseline) given.
top_strength: Rance caught the customer's offhand comment about the elevator being far from the unit on the destination side and folded it straight into the time estimate without missing a beat: "Yeah, that'll kind of come into play... to account for the fifth floor. And then, the walk at the other side and the elevator." That's good real-time judgment, not just reading a script.
coaching_note: This call reads like an inventory-confirmation checklist, not a sales or service call — you never once used the customer's name, and huge chunks of the standard walk (pricing breakdown, No Worries Damage Coverage, Meet Your Mover, On-Time Guarantee, Save Your Ass prep speech, email handoff) never came up at all. Even on a pre-move confirmation call, customers should hear the differentiators and get a reminder of how billing works — right now this customer has no idea what the hourly rate is or what's included. Start using the customer's name early and often, and build in a 60-second version of the pricing/differentiator rundown even when the booking is already made — it reinforces value and reduces day-of surprises.
phone_presence_notes: Polite and reassuring throughout (frequent 'sir,' calm handling of the loading-dock concern) but strictly transactional — moves item to item without ever using the customer's name or building rapport beyond the task.
